title: Standardizing Distributed Data Pipelines
business: A data engineering team managing a large-scale Python monorepo for distributed data pipelines.
problem: The team struggles with inconsistent code style and fragmented linting configurations across multiple sub-projects, leading to frequent CI failures and high cognitive load during code reviews.
solution: By adopting Ruff, the team consolidates multiple legacy tools into a single, unified configuration file, ensuring consistent formatting and linting rules across the entire repository structure.
steps: Install the Ruff package via pip within the virtual environment.
Create a root-level pyproject.toml file to define global linting and formatting standards.
Configure hierarchical settings to allow specific sub-directories to override global rules if necessary.
Integrate Ruff into the local development environment and CI/CD pipeline as a pre-commit hook.
Execute automatic error correction using the fix support feature to resolve existing style violations.
outcome: The team achieves a unified coding standard that reduces CI friction and simplifies the onboarding process for new developers, while maintaining high code quality across all pipeline modules.
limitation: Ruff's rapid development cycle means that new rules are frequently added; teams must monitor the configuration to ensure that enabling new preview rules does not inadvertently break existing, stable codebases.
